question: Drug A is an experimental compound being investigated for potential use as a protectant against venous thrombosis. Binding assays reveal that the drug’s primary mechanism of action is to block carboxylation of glutamic acid residues in certain serum proteins. Drug A is most similar to which of the following:?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Drug A -> blocks carboxylation of glutamic acid residues in certain serum proteins -> similar to Warfarin -> 80% CHAIN: Drug A -> blocks carboxylation of glutamic acid residues in certain serum proteins -> affects coagulation pathway -> similar to Heparin -> 70% CHAIN: Drug A -> blocks carboxylation of glutamic acid residues in certain serum proteins -> inhibits clot formation -> similar to Bivalirudin -> 80%
analysis: Drug A's mechanism of action of blocking carboxylation of glutamic acid residues in serum proteins indicates it is most similar to Warfarin, which also interferes with the carboxylation of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors.
